tools.name: microsoft_graph_get
tools.title: Microsoft graph get
tools.description:
Read Graph using GET. Call microsoft_graph_suggest_queries unless a fitting similar-intent result is in this conversation; if unhelpful, use microsoft_graph_list_properties unless the relevant schema is already visible.
Match the original request's operation, resource, relationship direction, conditions and result granularity. Related or inverse relationships, current-state summaries in place of history, and aggregates in place of records are not substitutes. Resolve required identifiers through supported reads or ask; never send placeholders or incomplete paths.
Adapt a fitting template for known values and user-requested conditions, retaining its other specialized paths, query options, headers and applicable API notes. Preserve predicates rather than replacing them with sort or page limits. When filtering locally, cover the relevant pages. Escape query literals and use literal ISO 8601 dates instead of now().
A valid empty collection answering the query is not an access failure. When a specific required resource remains inaccessible, request_access may apply if advertised.

relativeUrl.description: Fully resolved relative Graph URL for the requested resource and operation, with correctly quoted query literals and all required IDs; no placeholders or omitted segments. Use /beta for requests built from microsoft_graph_list_properties.

headers.description: Optional HTTP headers to forward to Microsoft Graph (e.g. ConsistencyLevel, Prefer, If-Match). Forward the `headers` map from the matched microsoft_graph_suggest_queries example when present. When a previous successful response includes an ETag, pass its exact value as If-Match on the next mutation of that resource. Reserved names (Authorization, Host, Content-Type, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, etc.) are silently dropped.

tools.name: microsoft_graph_list_properties
tools.title: Microsoft graph list properties
tools.description: Get the Graph beta schema for an entity or complex type when query discovery yields nothing useful, unless the schema is already visible. Properties come from the beta schema; use /beta for requests built from them. Returns property names and types, not proof of filter, sort or expand support; enum members are not included.

tools.name: microsoft_graph_suggest_queries
tools.title: Microsoft graph suggest queries
tools.description:
Find Graph request templates for the user's intent. Call before Graph execution unless a fitting similar-intent result is already in the conversation.
Determine the main task outside quoted text, code and pasted payloads. Preserve its explicit action verb, resource, relationship direction, subtype, conditions, requested properties and result granularity; descriptions of existing state do not authorize another operation. For an information question, describe retrieval of the requested resource or state.
Write a compact, reusable intentDescription: replace instance names, identifiers, URLs, literal values, dates and numeric thresholds with their locator or condition roles. Do not add inferred APIs, operations, outputs or implicit context.
Returns YAML suggestions with Score, RetrievalText and ordered Steps (method, pathAndQuery, body, headers and customInstructions). Compare each suggestion to the original user request, not just the score. API notes cannot override user intent or approval. Refine or split an unfitting intent. If no useful result remains, call microsoft_graph_list_properties unless the schema is already visible, then use verified schema and model knowledge for the appropriate method.

intentDescription.description: Compact retrieval phrase. Copy the main requested action verb, then summarize resources, relationships, locator kinds and conditions. Replace actual names, identifiers and filter values with their roles.

tools.name: request_access
tools.title: Request access
tools.description:
Request governed access needed for a specific task when the user asks for access, or when ANY tool, MCP server or service (not only Microsoft Graph) can't access a specific resource the task needs, e.g. Azure, Kusto, WorkIQ or Snowflake reporting 403 Forbidden, access denied, not authorized, insufficient privileges or a missing role.
Describe the intended access or task; this tool requests access rather than performing that operation.
The identity needing access may differ from the identity authenticated to this tool. In a human-user (HU) to agent-user (AU) flow, keep the HU as the authenticated requester; if the blocked operation ran as the HU's owned AU, explicitly set target.id to that AU's user object ID. Do not omit target and request HU self-access in that case. Establish the failed-operation identity from authoritative tool results or authentication context; don't assume every Azure call or 403 is an AU. If the identity or owned agent-user ID is unclear, resolve it through supported reads or ask rather than guessing.
Not for sign-in failures, policy restrictions, malformed requests, transient errors or empty general searches.
Call it directly, without microsoft_graph_suggest_queries. For governed access, the service resolves the resource and role or access package, then the tool asks the user to answer any clarifying questions and confirm the proposal; only that confirmation submits a request.
Without a continuation, each call starts a new Dynamic Access session. Resume only with a continuation returned by this tool; don't start another session to resume, poll, or retry after an unknown outcome or a user decline. Never create, clarify or submit these sessions with Graph write tools.
Clients supporting forms use elicitation. Otherwise, needs_clarification or needs_confirmation returns a prompt and continuationToken: present the prompt's questions, choices or full proposal in chat and wait for the user's response. Resume with unchanged original inputs and continuation containing that token, the user's action and clarification answers keyed by question ID. Use offered choice values; never invent answers or infer acceptance. Clarification answers do not submit anything; the resolved proposal requires a separate explicit confirmation. Omit answers for confirmation. Each token is single-use and expires after 30 minutes.
Report outcome, message, IDs and status. Submission isn't a grant: access is effective only when delivered. completed with accessPackageAssignmentRequestId means a handoff; that access-package assignment request governs approval and delivery.
Check status with microsoft_graph_get; neither a failed read nor an unknown outcome means no request exists. After a denial, don't seek the same access another way.
Once delivery is confirmed, retry the original operation through the original tool or MCP server as the same access-target identity, preserving the original operation inputs. Do not retry merely because the request is submitted or delivering. For an AU request, do not switch to HU or administrator credentials to make the operation succeed.

accessIntent.description: Resource to access and required operation, using actual details supplied by the user or a connected tool.

summarizedOriginalIntent.description: Concise summary of the originating user objective. Omit if unavailable.

requestedDuration.description: Requested positive XML Schema duration, expressing weeks as days. Omit if unspecified.

justification.description: The user's stated reason, or a factual reason from their objective. Omit if unavailable.

target.description: Agent user needing access on behalf of its human owner. Set this when the blocked operation ran as that owned agent user, even if this tool authenticates its human owner. Omit when requesting access for the authenticated caller.

id.description: Object ID of the owned agent user needing access, not its service principal or blueprint application.

continuation.description: Only for a conversational prompt returned by this tool when forms are unavailable. Copy continuationToken into token, set action to the user's explicit accept, decline or cancel, and supply answers only for clarification. Keep all original request inputs unchanged. Omit when starting a flow or responding through elicitation.

token.description: Single-use continuationToken returned by request_access. Copy unchanged.

action.description: User's response: accept, decline or cancel. Never infer acceptance.

answers.description: Clarification answers keyed by the returned question IDs, using offered choice values or user-provided text. Omit for confirmation.
